CE marking eligibility Blocked — 2 items to resolve Third-party required · Art 32(3). Support period to 2037-01-20. Readiness not assessed. Step 5: Annex I requirements not assessed for this product. Conformity assessment route Third-party required — self-attest is not sufficient; engage a notified body or obtain an EU cybersecurity certificate. Conformity assessment route (Art 32) Annex III · Class II Art 32(3) Third-party required Module B+C, Module H, or EU cybersecurity certificate ≥ substantial. Third-party assessment required — notified-body name + 4-digit number must populate Annex V §7 before issuing the DoC. Article 32 · Conformity assessment Module B + Module C — EU type-examination + production conformity Notified Body (B) examines a representative sample and issues an EU type-examination certificate. Manufacturer (C) ensures every produced unit conforms to the approved type. Procedure 1 Submit application + technical documentation + representative sample to a Notified Body. 2 Notified Body issues EU type-examination certificate (Module B). Valid for ≤ 5 years. 3 Implement Module C production-conformity controls; the NB number appears on the CE mark. 4 Inform the NB of every modification that may affect conformity; certificate may need updating. 5 Renew the certificate before expiry; retain it for at least 10 years after the last product is placed on market. Article 27 · Presumption of conformity Harmonised standards you're applying 2 selected Products in conformity with harmonised standards (or parts of them) whose references have been published in the Official Journal of the European Union are presumed to be in conformity with the corresponding essential requirements. Applying any of these in full enables Module A self-assessment for Annex III Class I. EN 18031-1Common security requirements for radio equipment (RED Article 3(3)(d/e/f)) EN 18031-2Network and child-safety related radio equipment EN 18031-3Radio equipment processing virtual money / monetary value IEC 62443-4-1Industrial automation — secure product development lifecycle IEC 62443-4-2Industrial automation — technical security for components ETSI EN 303 645Cybersecurity for consumer IoT ISO/SAE 21434Road vehicles — cybersecurity engineering ISO/IEC 27001Information security management systems ISO/IEC 15408 (Common Criteria)IT security evaluation — for products seeking certification Article 30 · How to affix the CE mark The physical marking rules Reg (EU) 2024/2847 Minimum height 5 mm — proportions of the official CE symbol preserved if the size is reduced. Affixed visibly, legibly and indelibly on the product. If the product's nature does not allow that, affix it on the packaging and on the accompanying documents. Affix the CE mark before the product is placed on the market — not after. Class II / Critical: place the notified body's four-digit identification number immediately after the CE mark, on the same surface and at the same minimum height. Marks that are likely to mislead third parties about the meaning or form of the CE mark are forbidden (other marks may appear if they don't impair the CE mark's visibility, legibility, or meaning). Annex VII bundle (.zip) JSON-LD Submit Article 13(2) · Substantial modification When you must re-run the conformity assessment A product that has been substantially modified is treated as a new product — it must undergo a fresh conformity assessment before being placed on the market again. Re-run this journey if any of the following changes: The intended purpose or the operational environment. The security properties advertised in Annex II §4 (essential functionality, security properties). Components or sub-systems whose modification affects the cybersecurity risk assessment per Art 13(2). The product is no longer covered by the harmonised standards or common specifications that supported its DoC. A safety-relevant or regulator-flagged vulnerability is resolved by an architectural change rather than a patch. Minor maintenance fixes and routine security patches typically do not qualify — but document the assessment so an auditor can see the call. CE marking eligibility Blocked — 2 items to resolve Third-party required · Art 32(3). Support period to 2037-01-20. Readiness not assessed. Step 5: Annex I requirements not assessed for this product. Conformity assessment route Third-party required — self-attest is not sufficient; engage a notified body or obtain an EU cybersecurity certificate. Conformity assessment route (Art 32) Annex III · Class II Art 32(3) Third-party required Module B+C, Module H, or EU cybersecurity certificate ≥ substantial. Third-party assessment required — notified-body name + 4-digit number must populate Annex V §7 before issuing the DoC. Article 32 · Conformity assessment Module B + Module C — EU type-examination + production conformity Notified Body (B) examines a representative sample and issues an EU type-examination certificate. Manufacturer (C) ensures every produced unit conforms to the approved type. Procedure 1 Submit application + technical documentation + representative sample to a Notified Body. 2 Notified Body issues EU type-examination certificate (Module B). Valid for ≤ 5 years. 3 Implement Module C production-conformity controls; the NB number appears on the CE mark. 4 Inform the NB of every modification that may affect conformity; certificate may need updating. 5 Renew the certificate before expiry; retain it for at least 10 years after the last product is placed on market. Article 27 · Presumption of conformity Harmonised standards you're applying 2 selected Products in conformity with harmonised standards (or parts of them) whose references have been published in the Official Journal of the European Union are presumed to be in conformity with the corresponding essential requirements. Applying any of these in full enables Module A self-assessment for Annex III Class I. Affixed visibly, legibly and indelibly on the product. If the product's nature does not allow that, affix it on the packaging and on the accompanying documents. Affix the CE mark before the product is placed on the market — not after. Class II / Critical: place the notified body's four-digit identification number immediately after the CE mark, on the same surface and at the same minimum height. Marks that are likely to mislead third parties about the meaning or form of the CE mark are forbidden (other marks may appear if they don't impair the CE mark's visibility, legibility, or meaning). Update delivery (Art 13(8)) Update channel Over-the-air (OTA) Package manager Customer portal Physical media Security updates are free of charge Art 13(8) — for the entire support period, at no cost to the user. Security updates shipped separately from features Annex I Part II §8 — users can take security fixes without unrelated functional changes. Automatic updates (Annex I Part I) Automatic security updates on by default Annex I §2(c) — secure-by-default delivery of security updates. Users can opt out of automatic updates Required where automatic updates are the default — the user stays in control. Users can postpone an update Operational continuity — defer, don't decline, a pending update. Default-on with opt-out — Annex I compliant. Single Sign-On (SAML / OIDC) DestroSolutions Not connected Let your team log in with your existing identity provider — Google Workspace, Microsoft Entra, Okta, or any SAML 2.0 / OIDC provider.
Microsoft 365 Microsoft Not connected One-click Microsoft 365 — connects Azure AD identity sync, then cascades to Teams, Outlook, OneDrive and SharePoint on demand.
Okta Not connected SCIM directory sync + SAML SSO. Pull member roles from your Okta org.
Azure AD Microsoft Not connected Standalone Azure AD without the M365 mail/Teams payload. Pure directory sync.
Auth0 Okta Not connected Auth0 tenant SSO + Management API user sync.
OneLogin One Identity Not connected SSO + provisioning via the OneLogin API.
Google Workspace Google Not connected One-click Google Workspace — directory sync, then cascades to Drive, Calendar, Meet and Gmail on demand.
Duo Security Cisco Not connected MFA + adaptive access. Push notifications, FIDO2 keys, device-trust signals. Pull authentication logs and policy state into the brain.
JumpCloud Not connected Cloud directory — users, devices, RADIUS, LDAP, SSO, MFA. Sync members and surface device-posture signals against your product fleet.
Slack Not connected Post advisories to a channel of your choice. Choose a default channel after connecting.
Microsoft Teams (Webhook) Microsoft Not connected Standalone Teams alerts via incoming webhook — use this if you don't want to grant Graph API access.
Discord Not connected Drop alerts into a Discord channel via incoming webhook.
PagerDuty Not connected Page on-call for active exploitation events. Uses Events API v2 routing key.
Opsgenie Atlassian Not connected Atlassian Opsgenie alerts via REST API integration key.
Mattermost Not connected Self-hosted Slack alternative. Route critical advisories + Article 14 deadline alerts into a Mattermost channel via incoming webhook.
T Microsoft Teams (Graph) Microsoft Not connected Post advisories into Teams channels via Microsoft Graph — uses the M365 OAuth token, no separate consent.
31 Google Calendar Google Not connected Auto-create calendar events for CRA Article 14 reporting deadlines and patch-Tuesday milestones.
Google Meet Google Not connected Spin up a Meet bridge automatically when a Severity-1 advisory escalates — pasted into the Teams/Slack alert.
Jira Cloud Atlassian Connected Turn CVE findings into Jira issues. Auto-link issue ID back to the PSIRT case.
ServiceNow Not connected Create ServiceNow incidents from PSIRT cases. ITSM record of truth for vulnerabilities.
Linear Not connected Convert CVEs to Linear issues with team + project routing.
Asana Not connected Push remediation tasks into your Asana project.
ClickUp Not connected ClickUp task creation with custom fields for CVE metadata.
Zendesk Not connected Open Zendesk tickets for customer-impacting vulnerabilities.
Freshdesk Freshworks Not connected Freshdesk ticket sync via the Freshworks API.
Notion Not connected Mirror PSIRT advisories into a Notion database. Roll-up by product, severity, and SLA.
Splunk Not connected Forward CVE events to Splunk HEC. Indexed under a configurable source type.
Microsoft Sentinel Microsoft Not connected Stream events into a Sentinel workspace via Data Collection Rule.
IBM QRadar IBM Not connected Forward events to QRadar via syslog or REST API offense create.
Sumo Logic Not connected Sumo Logic HTTP source ingestion for CVE events.
Datadog Not connected Datadog Security Signals + log forwarding via Datadog API key.
Elastic Security Elastic Not connected Ingest into an Elastic Security cluster via Elasticsearch ingest pipeline.
Google Chronicle Google Not connected Stream events to Chronicle via Ingestion API.
Sentry Functional Software Not connected Pull production error events and crash signals into the brain — correlate runtime exceptions with the CVE inventory.
PostHog Not connected Tap product-analytics events for behavioural anomaly detection (mass logout, sudden surge in failed auth, suspicious feature usage).
Cortex XSOAR Palo Alto Networks Not connected Trigger XSOAR playbooks on critical advisory ingestion.
Tines Not connected Fire a Tines story on every published advisory. Paste the webhook URL.
Torq Not connected Fire a Torq workflow on advisory + risk events.
Swimlane Not connected Swimlane Turbine SOAR integration.
Recorded Future Not connected Enrich CVEs with Recorded Future risk scores + threat actor context.
Mandiant Threat Intel Google Not connected Mandiant Advantage API for APT tracking and campaign analysis.
AlienVault OTX AT&T Cybersecurity Not connected Open Threat Exchange — pulse subscriptions + IOC enrichment.
ThreatConnect Not connected ThreatConnect Platform — threat intelligence + case management.
MISP MISP Project Not connected Self-hosted MISP instance — bi-directional IOC sharing.
Anomali ThreatStream Anomali Not connected Anomali ThreatStream feed ingestion + IOC enrichment.
CrowdStrike Falcon CrowdStrike Not connected Falcon Intel API — adversary profiles, eCrime indicators, IOCs.
VirusTotal Google Not connected VT Enterprise — file/url/IP/domain reputation enrichment.
Shodan Not connected Shodan attack-surface enrichment for exposed services.
Anthropic Claude Anthropic Not connected Route the PCTI brain's reasoning chain through Claude — use your own Anthropic key so requests don't hit our quota.
NVIDIA NIM NVIDIA Not connected Self-hosted NIM endpoint for the embedding + classification heads of the PCTI brain. GPU-accelerated, on-prem-friendly.
Tenable.io Tenable Not connected Pull Tenable.io scan results and re-prioritise via PCTI scoring.
Nessus Professional Tenable Not connected On-prem Nessus scanner results via Nessus REST API.
Qualys VMDR Qualys Not connected Qualys VMDR findings + asset inventory via Cloud Platform API.
Rapid7 InsightVM Rapid7 Not connected InsightVM risk findings + Insight Platform asset sync.
Snyk Not connected Reachability analysis from your Snyk Open Source data. Reduces false positives by ~70%. Reachability · −70% false positives
Endor Labs Not connected Enterprise reachability + provenance from Endor Labs. Reduces false positives by ~80%. Reachability · enterprise tier
Wiz Not connected Wiz CNAPP findings + cloud workload posture.
Orca Security Not connected Orca Cloud Security Platform findings ingestion.
Lacework Not connected Lacework Polygraph cloud security findings.
Veracode Not connected SAST + DAST + SCA platform. Pull static-analysis findings, dynamic-scan results, and policy compliance state per application.
Checkmarx One Checkmarx Not connected AST platform — SAST · SCA · IaC security · container security · API security. Pull findings and policy violations into the brain.
JFrog Xray JFrog Not connected Universal binary scanner — Maven · npm · PyPI · Go · NuGet · Docker · Helm — integrated with Artifactory. Pull violations + license posture.
SentinelOne Not connected Endpoint detection + response. Pull threat detections, agent inventory, vulnerability inventory (Ranger). Surface device exposure against your products.
Microsoft Defender for Endpoint Microsoft Not connected MDE — endpoint EDR + threat & vulnerability management. Pull TVM findings, device exposure score, ASR rule violations into the brain.
GitHub Connected Ingest Dependabot alerts and SBOMs from selected repos.
GitLab Not connected GitLab Vulnerability Reports + dependency scanning artefacts.
Bitbucket Atlassian Not connected Bitbucket Cloud security reports + Pipelines findings.
Jenkins Not connected Block Jenkins pipelines on active exploitation CVEs. Paste the webhook URL.
CircleCI Not connected CircleCI orb to gate builds on CVE policy.
GitHub Actions GitHub Not connected GitHub Action to gate workflows on CVE policy. Requires the GitHub OAuth app.
AWS Security Hub AWS Not connected Push findings to Security Hub via BatchImportFindings using an IAM access key.
Google Security Command Center Google Not connected Surface CVE findings as SCC findings via the Security Command Center API.
Microsoft Defender for Cloud Microsoft Not connected Azure Defender CSPM findings + Azure Resource Graph asset queries.
AWS GuardDuty AWS Not connected AWS threat-detection service. Pull GuardDuty findings (recon, malware, compromised credentials, crypto-mining) and correlate against your fleet.
Prisma Cloud (Twistlock) Palo Alto Networks Not connected CSPM + CWPP — container image scanning, Kubernetes runtime defence, IaC security, CIEM. Pull alert + compliance state.
Aqua Security Aqua Not connected Cloud-native security — image scanning, runtime protection, Kubernetes admission control. Pull image-vuln + runtime-incident state.
Sysdig Secure Sysdig Not connected Container + Kubernetes + cloud security — runtime detection (Falco), image scanning, posture. Pull policy violations + runtime alerts.
Gmail Google Not connected Send CVE digests via the Gmail API on behalf of an org mailbox.
SMTP / Custom mail server Generic Not connected Send digests through your own SMTP relay. Supports STARTTLS + SMTPS.
R Resend Not connected Send advisory digests, regulator notifications, and customer comms via Resend's transactional API.
O Outlook Microsoft Not connected Send PSIRT advisory emails on behalf of your tenant via Microsoft Graph Mail.Send.
CSV Export destrosolutions Not connected Download advisory + finding rollups as CSV. Configure a presigned download token.
JSON Export destrosolutions Not connected Raw JSON export of findings + assets. Same data model as the API.
STIX 2.1 OASIS Not connected STIX 2.1 bundles for downstream TAXII consumers.
CSAF 2.0 OASIS Not connected Common Security Advisory Framework 2.0 docs for PSIRT distribution.
OneDrive Microsoft Not connected Export evidence packs (CSAF, SBOM, audit logs) into your tenant's OneDrive — addressable by SharePoint paths.
Google Drive Google Not connected Export evidence packs to your shared Workspace drive — uses the Google Workspace OAuth token.
NVD NVD / NIST CVE NIST Platform feed Built-in. NIST National Vulnerability Database — CVE + CVSS v3.1 enrichment.
KEV CISA KEV CISA Platform feed Built-in. CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog.
FIRST FIRST EPSS FIRST Not connected Built-in. Exploit Prediction Scoring System — 30-day exploit probability.
ATT&CK MITRE ATT&CK MITRE Not connected Built-in. MITRE ATT&CK Enterprise + ICS technique mapping.
OSV OSV.dev Google Platform feed Built-in. Open Source Vulnerabilities — schema-aligned advisories across PyPI, npm, Maven, Go, RubyGems, NuGet, Packagist, OSS-Fuzz, Linux distros.
GitHub Security Advisories GitHub Not connected Built-in. GHSA database — curated advisories for npm, pip, Maven, RubyGems, NuGet, Composer, Go, Rust, Pub.
ENISA EUVD ENISA Platform feed Built-in. European Union Vulnerability Database — EU-curated CVE feed with regional advisories. Connector live, full schema pending public spec.
CSAF advisories OASIS Not connected Built-in. Ingest Common Security Advisory Framework (CSAF 2.0) feeds from Red Hat, Cisco, Siemens, Bosch, Oracle and other vendor PSIRTs.
OpenCTI Filigran Not connected Self-hosted threat-intel platform. Pull STIX 2.1 indicators, reports, threat actors, and campaigns into the brain via the OpenCTI GraphQL API.
CIRCL Vulnerability Lookup CIRCL Not connected Built-in. CIRCL aggregator over NVD + CSAF + GHSA + EUVD — sub-second lookup API with vendor + CPE normalisation.
Microsoft MSRC Microsoft Not connected Built-in. Microsoft Security Response Center — Patch Tuesday advisories, Windows / Office / Azure / .NET CVEs.
Cisco PSIRT openVuln Cisco Not connected Cisco PSIRT openVuln API — IOS / IOS XE / NX-OS / WebEx / Meraki advisories with CVE + CVSS + workarounds.
Apple Security Updates Apple Not connected Built-in. macOS · iOS · iPadOS · watchOS · tvOS · Safari security advisories with CVE references.
Oracle Critical Patch Update Oracle Not connected Built-in. Oracle quarterly CPU — Java / Oracle DB / MySQL / WebLogic / E-Business Suite advisories.
SAP Security Notes SAP Not connected SAP Patch Day Security Notes — ABAP / NetWeaver / HANA / S/4HANA / SuccessFactors advisories.
VMware Security Advisories VMware (Broadcom) Not connected Built-in. VMSAs across vSphere · vCenter · ESXi · NSX · Tanzu · Workspace ONE · Carbon Black with CVSS v3.1.
Snyk Vulnerability DB Snyk Not connected Snyk's curated OSS vulnerability database — npm / pip / Maven / RubyGems / NuGet / Go / Composer / Hex / Pub with exploit maturity scoring.
Sonatype OSS Index Sonatype Not connected Built-in. Free OSS vulnerability index keyed by PURL — Maven / npm / NuGet / PyPI / Composer / RubyGems / RPM / DEB.
VulnCheck KEV+ VulnCheck Not connected Commercial KEV expansion — earlier KEV-equivalent labelling, exploit chain enrichment, ransomware actor attribution.
abuse.ch URLHaus abuse.ch Not connected Built-in. Malware-distribution URLs with payload + threat-actor attribution. Feed updates every 5 minutes.
AbuseIPDB Not connected Crowd-sourced IP-reputation database. Pull abuse confidence scores into the IOC store for correlation with detection signals.
JPCERT / JVN JPCERT/CC Not connected Built-in. Japan Vulnerability Notes — APAC-region advisories from JPCERT/CC and IPA. Bridges CVE numbering with JVN/JVNDB IDs.
HackerOne Not connected Bug bounty + VDP platform. Pull triaged reports, severity, CVSS, repro details into the PSIRT queue with auto-CVE mapping.
Bugcrowd Not connected Crowdsourced security platform — bug bounty, pen-test-as-a-service, attack-surface management. Pull validated submissions into PSIRT.

Authorise GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, or Azure DevOps, pick the repos you ship from, and every push runs an SBOM + CVE scan. No YAML, no runner setup. Quick start Auto-scan GitHub DestroSec GitHub App. Auto-scan on push and pull_request. SBOM + CVE findings flow into the platform automatically. 2 repos tracked Connect OAuth only GitLab OAuth supported. visibleText: D Product Security OS DestroSolutions Home Products Friday Inbox Chats Projects Run history Security Vulnerabilities Threat intel PSIRT Supply chain Compliance Workspace Reports Integrations Settings Search products, CVEs, playbooks… Ctrl K SS Singh Admin INTEGRATIONS CI/CD quick start Upload SBOMs from your pipeline 1 · Create an API key Give it the upload and read scopes. Open API keys 2 · Save it as a CI secret Name it DESTRO_API_KEY — GitHub: Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions. GitLab: Settings → CI/CD → Variables (masked). 3 · Add the job Product name in DestroSolutions API address: https://iaxxugiyicroptkuhgyj.supabase.co/functions/v1/api-gateway GitHub Actions GitLab CI Add to .gitlab-ci.yml destrosolutions-sbom: stage: test image: alpine:3.20 variables: DESTRO_API: "https://iaxxugiyicroptkuhgyj.supabase.co/functions/v1/api-gateway" PRODUCT_NAME: "My product" PRODUCT_VERSION: "$CI_COMMIT_REF_NAME" before_script: - apk add --no-cache curl jq - curl -sSfL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anchore/syft/main/install.sh | sh -s -- -b /usr/local/bin script: - syft dir:. -o cyclonedx-json=sbom.cdx.json - | set -eu q() { jq -rn --arg v "$1" '$v|@uri'; } curl -sS --fail-with-body -X POST \ "$DESTRO_API/api/v1/sbom/upload?product_name=$(q "$PRODUCT_NAME")&product_version=$(q "$PRODUCT_VERSION")&file_name=sbom.cdx.json" \ -H "X-API-Key: $DESTRO_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ --data-binary @sbom.cdx.json -o upload.json || { cat upload.json; echo; exit 1; } IMPORT_ID=$(jq -r .data.import_id upload.json) echo "Uploaded, scan $IMPORT_ID" for i in $(seq 1 60); do curl -sS --fail-with-body "$DESTRO_API/api/v1/scans/$IMPORT_ID" -H "X-API-Key: $DESTRO_API_KEY" -o scan.json || { cat scan.json; echo; exit 1; } [ "$(jq -r .data.finished scan.json)" = "true" ] && break sleep 10 done jq .data scan.json [ "$(jq -r .data.status scan.json)" = "completed" ] || { echo "Scan not completed"; exit 1; } CRITICAL=$(jq -r .data.product_findings_by_severity.critical scan.json) echo "Critical findings on this product: $CRITICAL" [ "$CRITICAL" -eq 0 ] # DESTRO_API_KEY: add it under Settings → CI/CD → Variables (masked). Copy The job uploads the SBOM to the product version named after the branch or tag, waits for matching to finish, and fails when the product has critical findings. RESPONSE GUIDES Guide Use when From severity Steps Your checklist KEV-listed CVE detected on production Any active product matches a CVE on the CISA KEV catalogue Critical 6 Not started Supply-chain compromise of a dependency Upstream maintainer takeover, malicious release, or unmaintained-package signal High 5 Not started Zero-day disclosure coming public Researcher tips you off ahead of a public release, or you're cc'd on a CERT pre-disclosure Critical 6 Not started High-severity bug-bounty submission HackerOne / Bugcrowd report with CVSS ≥ 7.0 High 6 Not started Customer-reported security incident Customer security team escalates a finding from their own scanners or audits High 5 Not started Active compromise suspected (IR-grade) Internal detection or external tip suggesting active exploitation Critical 5 Not started KEV-LISTED CVE DETECTED ON PRODUCTION Start checklist 1. Confirm exposure on the affected product Open Products → the affected product → Vulnerabilities. Confirm the CVE row is present and tagged KEV. Detect · Security analyst 2. Open a PSIRT case PSIRT → Cases → New case. Severity = critical. Source = internal_scan. Link the CVE id. Investigate · PSIRT lead 3. Notify customer-facing channels Post to #cs-security and #sales-eng. Use the standard KEV alert template. Communicate · PSIRT comms 4. Apply mitigation or shutdown Patch path on the CVE drawer. If patch can't ship in 24h, evaluate WAF rule or feature-flag shutdown. If yes: Patch shipped → step 5. If no: Shutdown path → step 5 (with note). Remediate · Engineering 5. Draft and publish a customer advisory Promote the case to an advisory. Set status to in_review, get sign-off, publish. Communicate · PSIRT lead 6. Post-mortem within 5 business days Document what we caught, what we missed, and the auto-detect we'll add for next time. RESPONSE GUIDES Guide Use when From severity Steps Your checklist KEV-listed CVE detected on production Any active product matches a CVE on the CISA KEV catalogue Critical 6 Not started Supply-chain compromise of a dependency Upstream maintainer takeover, malicious release, or unmaintained-package signal High 5 Not started Zero-day disclosure coming public Researcher tips you off ahead of a public release, or you're cc'd on a CERT pre-disclosure Critical 6 Not started High-severity bug-bounty submission HackerOne / Bugcrowd report with CVSS ≥ 7.0 High 6 Not started Customer-reported security incident Customer security team escalates a finding from their own scanners or audits High 5 Not started Active compromise suspected (IR-grade) Internal detection or external tip suggesting active exploitation Critical 5 Not started KEV-LISTED CVE DETECTED ON PRODUCTION Start checklist 1. Confirm exposure on the affected product Open Products → the affected product → Vulnerabilities. Confirm the CVE row is present and tagged KEV. Detect · Security analyst 2. Open a PSIRT case PSIRT → Cases → New case. Severity = critical. Source = internal_scan. Link the CVE id. Investigate · PSIRT lead 3. Notify customer-facing channels Post to #cs-security and #sales-eng. Use the standard KEV alert template. Communicate · PSIRT comms 4. Apply mitigation or shutdown Patch path on the CVE drawer. If patch can't ship in 24h, evaluate WAF rule or feature-flag shutdown. If yes: Patch shipped → step 5. If no: Shutdown path → step 5 (with note). Remediate · Engineering 5. Draft and publish a customer advisory Promote the case to an advisory. Set status to in_review, get sign-off, publish. Communicate · PSIRT lead 6. Post-mortem within 5 business days Document what we caught, what we missed, and the auto-detect we'll add for next time. Confirm exposure on the affected product Open Products → the affected product → Vulnerabilities. Confirm the CVE row is present and tagged KEV. Detect · Security analyst 2. Open a PSIRT case PSIRT → Cases → New case. Severity = critical. Source = internal_scan. Link the CVE id. Investigate · PSIRT lead 3. Notify customer-facing channels Post to #cs-security and #sales-eng. Use the standard KEV alert template. Communicate · PSIRT comms 4. Apply mitigation or shutdown Patch path on the CVE drawer. Draft and publish a customer advisory Promote the case to an advisory. Set status to in_review, get sign-off, publish. Communicate · PSIRT lead 6. Confirm exposure on the affected product Open Products → the affected product → Vulnerabilities. Confirm the CVE row is present and tagged KEV. Detect · Security analyst 2. Open a PSIRT case PSIRT → Cases → New case. Severity = critical. Source = internal_scan. Link the CVE id. Investigate · PSIRT lead 3. Notify customer-facing channels Post to #cs-security and #sales-eng. Use the standard KEV alert template. Communicate · PSIRT comms 4. Apply mitigation or shutdown Patch path on the CVE drawer. Draft and publish a customer advisory Promote the case to an advisory. Set status to in_review, get sign-off, publish. Communicate · PSIRT lead 6. RESPONSE GUIDES Guide Use when From severity Steps Your checklist KEV-listed CVE detected on production Any active product matches a CVE on the CISA KEV catalogue Critical 6 Not started Supply-chain compromise of a dependency Upstream maintainer takeover, malicious release, or unmaintained-package signal High 5 Not started Zero-day disclosure coming public Researcher tips you off ahead of a public release, or you're cc'd on a CERT pre-disclosure Critical 6 Not started High-severity bug-bounty submission HackerOne / Bugcrowd report with CVSS ≥ 7.0 High 6 Not started Customer-reported security incident Customer security team escalates a finding from their own scanners or audits High 5 Not started Active compromise suspected (IR-grade) Internal detection or external tip suggesting active exploitation Critical 5 Not started KEV-LISTED CVE DETECTED ON PRODUCTION Start checklist 1. Confirm exposure on the affected product Open Products → the affected product → Vulnerabilities. Confirm the CVE row is present and tagged KEV. Detect · Security analyst 2. Open a PSIRT case PSIRT → Cases → New case. Severity = critical. Source = internal_scan. Link the CVE id. Investigate · PSIRT lead 3. Notify customer-facing channels Post to #cs-security and #sales-eng. Use the standard KEV alert template. Communicate · PSIRT comms 4. Apply mitigation or shutdown Patch path on the CVE drawer. If patch can't ship in 24h, evaluate WAF rule or feature-flag shutdown. If yes: Patch shipped → step 5. If no: Shutdown path → step 5 (with note). Remediate · Engineering 5. Draft and publish a customer advisory Promote the case to an advisory. Set status to in_review, get sign-off, publish. Communicate · PSIRT lead 6. Post-mortem within 5 business days Document what we caught, what we missed, and the auto-detect we'll add for next time. Draft and publish a customer advisory Promote the case to an advisory. Set status to in_review, get sign-off, publish. Communicate · PSIRT lead 6. Confirm exposure on the affected product Open Products → the affected product → Vulnerabilities. Confirm the CVE row is present and tagged KEV. Detect · Security analyst 2. Draft and publish a customer advisory Promote the case to an advisory. Set status to in_review, get sign-off, publish. Communicate · PSIRT lead 6. RESPONSE GUIDES Guide Use when From severity Steps Your checklist KEV-listed CVE detected on production Any active product matches a CVE on the CISA KEV catalogue Critical 6 Not started Supply-chain compromise of a dependency Upstream maintainer takeover, malicious release, or unmaintained-package signal High 5 Not started Zero-day disclosure coming public Researcher tips you off ahead of a public release, or you're cc'd on a CERT pre-disclosure Critical 6 Not started High-severity bug-bounty submission HackerOne / Bugcrowd report with CVSS ≥ 7.0 High 6 Not started Customer-reported security incident Customer security team escalates a finding from their own scanners or audits High 5 Not started Active compromise suspected (IR-grade) Internal detection or external tip suggesting active exploitation Critical 5 Not started KEV-LISTED CVE DETECTED ON PRODUCTION Start checklist 1. Confirm exposure on the affected product Open Products → the affected product → Vulnerabilities. Confirm the CVE row is present and tagged KEV. Detect · Security analyst 2. Open a PSIRT case PSIRT → Cases → New case. Severity = critical. Source = internal_scan. Link the CVE id. Investigate · PSIRT lead 3. Notify customer-facing channels Post to #cs-security and #sales-eng. Use the standard KEV alert template. Communicate · PSIRT comms 4. Apply mitigation or shutdown Patch path on the CVE drawer. If patch can't ship in 24h, evaluate WAF rule or feature-flag shutdown. If yes: Patch shipped → step 5. If no: Shutdown path → step 5 (with note). Remediate · Engineering 5. Draft and publish a customer advisory Promote the case to an advisory. Set status to in_review, get sign-off, publish. Communicate · PSIRT lead 6. Post-mortem within 5 business days Document what we caught, what we missed, and the auto-detect we'll add for next time.
